content:
ash: Shift sync — I'm handing off now. Quick summary: regen-worker backlog spiked (~3k jobs) around 18:12 UTC but consumer churned through it after we scaled the vectorization-worker. KV cache ops look normal. No active P0s, a couple P1 follow-ups left.

ben: +1. Action taken: scaled vector-worker to 5 replicas, restarted prefetcher, bumped redis pool to 80. Logs showed a burst of duplicate jobs from the ingestion pipeline. Root cause looks like a retry loop from an edge timeout. :mag:

oncall-bot: Alert resolved: regen-queue-depth > 2000 -> cleared at 18:27 UTC. Incident ID: INC-2025-438. Related alerts: redis-conns-high (suppressed).

tara: FYI I opened PR #2145 to add a dedup key on ingestion; CI passed but need one more reviewer. @ben can you take a look? Small change, tests cover retry path.

ben: Will review in ~30m. Also left a note in the PR about falling back to noop when prefetcher times out.

sam: Quick check — are there any regional fallbacks still enabled for eu-west? I saw a routing spike in logs earlier.

ash: EU fallback was toggled off at 18:35 UTC (we were failing over incorrectly). I pushed a short-lived patch to routing to prefer same-region and reverted after queue dropped. Patch: `route-policy: prefer-local` rollback applied.

ivy: I verified the KV eviction rate stayed within SLO during the spike. Metrics: eviction/sec peaked at 12 (SLO 30).

ben: Small follow-ups for next shift: 1) merge PR #2145 and deploy canary to prod, 2) add circuit-breaker on prefetcher (issue #322), 3) run a targeted replay for the duplicate jobs window to validate dedup.

ash: Leaving notes in the oncall doc. My contact if anything: DM or call. :phone: Next shift please watch regen-queue depth + redis connections for 12:00–19:00 window. Thanks — leaving now. :v:
